blocks.text: A basic need of industry is the maximum yield of a product, and the concept of equilibrium shows how to obtain it. Two reversible reactions of great industrial importance are the synthesis of ammonia by the Haber process and the preparation of sulfur trioxide for sulfuric acid by the contact process; both are exothermic gas reactions whose conditions are chosen by Le Chatelier's principle together with the need for a reasonable rate.

blocks.alt: Left: a graph of ammonia yield against temperature with five falling curves for 10 to 1000 atm, the higher pressures higher, and a dashed circle marking industrial conditions near 400 degrees C and 200 to 300 atm. Right: a blue box with the ammonia Kc values from 200 to 800 K and the optimum conditions, and an orange box with the SO3 table of temperature, Kc and mole per cent and the contact process conditions.
blocks.caption: Yield against temperature and pressure for the Haber process, and the SO3 equilibrium of the contact process (original diagram after Figure 8.4 and Tables 8.1 and 8.2; curves schematic).
blocks.long_description: The yield of ammonia is highest at low temperature and high pressure, reaching 98.3 per cent at 200 degrees C and 1000 atm, but at low temperature the reaction is too slow, so industry works near 400 degrees C at 200 to 300 atm with an iron catalyst. The ammonia Kc falls from 7.15 x 10^15 at 200 K to 3.96 x 10^-2 at 800 K. For sulfur trioxide Kc falls from 5500 at 200 degrees C to 13 at 700 degrees C and the yield from 98 to 31 per cent, so the gases pass over vanadium pentoxide at 1 atm and are recycled at 400 to 500 degrees C.
